what: Adversarial verification (3 agents) of the second-pass parity fixes: swap accounting, H4 boundary read, per-day add counting, profit-lock latch. One confirmed finding (EA suspends the trend-flip flatten while profit-locked) was FIXED in the same commit; swap accounting verified clean (ledger reconciles with balance).

confirmed_findings.title: EA suspends trend-change flatten while profit-locked; Python still flattens
confirmed_findings.claim: In OnTick the trend-change close is gated by accountSafe: `if(units > 0 && accountSafe)` where CheckAccountGuard() returns false once the daily profit lock latches (mq5:361-367). So on a locked day the EA does NOT flatten on an EMA-stack flip - units keep riding on their BE/trail stops (ManagePositions runs unconditionally) until stop-out, weekend close, or the next day's unlock. Python's flip-flatten at py:704-709 runs unconditionally, exiting at the flip bar's open even when profit_locked_today is set. The same suppression applies to the EA's equity-floor lock, but there the position is flattened anyway, so only the profit-lock path diverges.
confirmed_findings.impact: On days where the lock latches (net day gain >= 1% of initial, i.e. exactly the strategy's best days) and the H1 EMA50/200 stack then flips, Python realizes the exit a full locked-window earlier than the EA would. Exit-path divergences were the load-bearing finding of the prior audits (H1 exits ~16R), so the screen's exit stream is not EA-faithful on locked days: different exit prices, possible extra overnight holds and swap EA-side, and next-day state differences. Low frequency (strong-win day + same-day trend flip) but a genuine unmodeled EA behavior on the exact code path this branch claims parity for.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning: CONFIRMED, not refuted. EA: FTMOQuantEA.mq5:1033 gates the only trend-flip close (`CloseAllUnits("trend change")`) behind `units > 0 && accountSafe`, where CheckAccountGuard (mq5:361-368) latches tradingLocked=true and returns false for the rest of the day once TodayClosedPnl() >= initialBalance*InpDailyProfitLockPct/100 (default 1.0, active); the lock path returns false WITHOUT flattening (unlike the equity-floor path, which calls EmergencyFlatten at mq5:354-358), tradingLocked resets only at the next day rollover (RefreshDailyState mq5:164), OnTimer has no flip logic, and ManagePositions (mq5:737+, runs unconditionally at mq5:1022) only does TP1/TP2 partials/BE/trail — so on a profit-locked day the EA holds units through an EMA-stack flip. Python: ftmo_quant_backtest.py:703-709 flattens on the flip gated only by `if units:`; profit_locked_today (py:650-654) gates only entry_ready (py:659). Executed a concrete scenario (scratchpad lock_flip_demo.py): with daily_profit_lock_pct=0.05 ($50 threshold), TP1 banks +$1,907 at 2024-01-03 03:00 (lock latches), the runner survives at break-even, and the engine still books a trend_change exit at 10:30 the SAME locked day (102.800) — bit-identical time/price to a run with the lock effectively disabled — while provably refusing a fresh 12:00 entry that day (proof the lock was active in-engine at the flip bar). So Python realizes the flip exit on locked days that the EA would defer to stop-out/weekend/next-day unlock, an unmodeled EA behavior on the exit path this parity branch (change #4, entry-side lock latch only) claims to mirror. Only trivial imprecision: EA compares TodayClosedPnl() vs Python's balance - day_start_balance, equivalent within the engine's model. Low frequency (needs a >=1%-gain day plus a same-day H1 EMA50/200 flip) but genuine divergence with different exit prices, possible extra overnight swap, and next-day state differences EA-side.
